cvEn:
Yaakov (Yankale) Cohen, son of Sara and Pinhas, was born in 1908 in Haifa to a family of workers. His father was the beadle of the first Ashkenazi synagogue in Haifa, "Hadrat Kodesh". Yaakov studied at the traditional *heder* and at the elementary school founded by the Alliance, and later worked as a carpenter's apprentice. From his youth he was a member of HaNoar HaOved in Haifa, and afterward he joined the Poalei Zion party. At a young age he came to Kfar Gil'adi, where he worked as a shepherd on the farm. There everyone knew him as a loyal and dedicated member who spoke little and did much.

In 1936 he joined the Haganah, and he served in its ranks for the rest of his life. In 1936 he went up with the "Shneorson group" to Kfar Etzion and took part in its defense. When Kfar Etzion was dismantled, he returned to his kibbutz.

In 1937 he enlisted in the Notrim. On 24 Tevet 5699 (15 January 1939), serving as deputy squad commander, he travelled with a group of Notrim from Kfar Gil'adi to the kibbutz's fields in Hamara, near the Lebanese border. On their return journey they were ambushed by a gang of smugglers who had crossed the border. Three shots struck Yaakov in the throat, and he died a few minutes later. His comrades engaged the gang, and with the help of an army platoon that arrived from Tel Hai they drove it back across the border. Yaakov was killed one day before he was to have married the woman he had chosen. He was laid to rest in the cemetery of Kfar Gil'adi. He left behind his parents and a brother.
